semantics: bounded parametric trajectories as first-class procedural state: per-instance finite programs of Linear (constant velocity / exact hold) and Accel (constant acceleration, discrete integer semantics pos += v; v += a, closed form D(t) = t*v0 + a*t*(t-1)/2) segments, stepped once per AdvanceTrajectories; wire tags 0x2b (SetTrajectory) and 0x2c (AdvanceTrajectories); empty program = deactivation; trajectory and translation state on one instance are mutually exclusive. Trajectory collapse (section 43): a maximal run of single-SetPosition interval groups is rewritten into one SetTrajectory descriptor plus per-frame AdvanceTrajectories only when the rebuilt stream decodes byte-identically to the original (normative proof) and is strictly smaller (complete cost falls).

notes: Collapse acceptance requires (1) exactness proven by normative decode of the rebuilt stream versus the original, and (2) strictly fewer total bytes. The encoder never trusts a fitted hypothesis from appearance.
SetPosition runs shorter than 3 frames cannot pay for a trajectory descriptor and are left alone (measured by the byte gate).
Exact integer semantics only; no floating point anywhere in the normative path.
A trajectory deactivates exactly when its final segment's steps are exhausted; the instance then stays at its final position (the unchanged lane resumes).
Per-frame representation costs on motion: SetPosition 26 B/frame, trajectory steady-state 14 B/frame (13 B interval envelope + 1 B advance) plus one amortized descriptor.
